title: Chunked Processing
prompt: Read a large CSV in chunks and calculate a summary without concatenating all raw chunks.
scenario: Use the synthetic data described below to practise c, h, u, n, k, e, d,  , c, s, v,  , a, n, d,  , a, g, g, r, e, g, a, t, i, o, n. Do not assume the input is correct without validating it.

starter.dataset_note: Use small synthetic in-memory data; do not place private or real customer data in exercises.

input_schema.description: Create or use a synthetic DataFrame with only the columns needed for this exercise.
validation: Document expected columns and data types.
State how missing values or duplicates should be treated.

expected_output: Read chunk by chunk using an explicit size.
Aggregate the chunk and combine partial aggregates.
Compare the result against a whole-file result on a small test input.

public_tests.name: normal-case
public_tests.description: The solution returns the required columns and correctly computes the stated result.

public_tests.name: edge-case
public_tests.description: The solution documents behavior for a missing value, duplicate key, empty input, invalid value, or other relevant edge case.

hints: Write down the expected result before coding.
Use Pandas operations that preserve labels unless position-based behavior is intended.
Add a small assertion for the most important property.
acceptance_criteria: Read chunk by chunk using an explicit size.
Aggregate the chunk and combine partial aggregates.
Compare the result against a whole-file result on a small test input.

grading_config.note: The generic short-response grader is only an initial scaffold; a reviewed isolated Python grader is required for automatic execution of arbitrary learner code.

status_note: Review prompt, starter, rubric, and server-side grading before publication.
